recipes.name: Holiday Dressing
ingredients_raw: 16 slices white bread, torn into pieces

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Grease an 8-inch square baking pan.
Make the cornbread: Combine cornbread mix, milk, and egg in a small bowl; stir until well blended. Pour batter into the prepared baking pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 15 to 19 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool. Lower the oven temperature to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

While the cornbread is cooking, make the dressing: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook onions, celery, and bell pepper in the melted butter until tender but not brown. Remove from the heat; do not drain.
At the same time, cook sausage in another large skillet over medium-high heat until evenly browned. Remove from the heat.
Crumble cooled cornbread into a food processor. Add bread pieces and pulse until crumbly. Transfer mixture to a large bowl.

Add sage, thyme, poultry seasoning, salt, and pepper to the cornbread mixture. Mix in parsley, cooked vegetables, and sausage with pan drippings. Stir in chicken stock and eggs; it will be a bit mushy.
Grease a 9x13-inch baking pan and fill with cornbread dressing.
Bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Holiday Dressing
raw_recipe.description: This holiday stuffing recipe was shared by my friend. I have used it for over fifteen years. No other dressing will serve the purpose, according to my son.

review.reviewBody:
Very good recipe. Thanks for sharing. The only change I made was to use an 8" skillet of cornbread (in the South we don't use cornbread mix lol) I think it needs just a slight bit of tweaking to be perfect. #1--is mushy, so I think the cooking temp should be brought up to at least 350­° & possibly reduce the broth by 1/2 - 1 cup; #2--needs a bit more sage flavor, next time I will either increase sage by 1 tsp or use sage flavored sausage. (p.s..for those leaving out the green bell pepper, you are missing out on some great flavor, just chop it really fine & you will not know it is there)

Update: I remade this recipe; I decreased the chicken broth to 3 cups, upped the sage to 1 tablespoon, used sage sausage, & upped the cooking temp to 350. IMHO those changes have made the dressing perfect (& now 5 star rated).

really good. used only 3C of broth and sage sausage as others indicated. also, used 2 packets of cornbread and 1/2 the white bread. made it faster by chopping everything in food processor to saute then using it to mix seasonings, eggs, and some broth (all of it would spill over).

I made exactly as written and made the cornbread. The stuffing was sweet which I did not care for and the cornbread gave it gritty texture. Our family recipe uses cooled mashed potatoes instead of cornbread in our dressing. I made again substituting 4 cups of crumbled and cooled mashed potatoes for the cornbread and it came out beautifully. Followed everything else exactly and it was great.

I used this recipe the very first time I made Thanksgiving dinner as a married woman and mom 20+ years ago and with just 1 or 2 modifications to perfect it for myself, THIS IS THE MOST DELICIOUS DRESSING ANY OF MY FRIENDS / FAMILY have ever had! This has been served not only at home, but numerous Thanksgiving potluck dinners, including the culinary staff at Disney's Grand Floridian Resort & Spa. My modifications: Double up on the sausage. Those bites loaded with sausage are the best! Less broth. I found the 4 cups made the pan way too mushy. I cut by 1 or 1 1/2 cups. Not really a modification but I don't care for large chunks / crunchy celery and onions. These, along with the green pepper are a staple for the best flavor in this recipe, so I chop really small and cook in the butter until there is no 'crunch' left in the celery/onions. I add the green pepper to sauté after a bit because I don't mind them still being a little firm. If you are new to dressing/stuffing, or just looking for something new, PLEASE try this! It's easy enough to add/take away to make it your own if you so desire!!!

Great recipe! As some of the other comments suggested, chicken broth is based on preference. I did the full 4, mixing in a 1/2 cup at a time. I enjoyed it, but will probably reduce to 3 cups next time. I also left out the pepper and added mushrooms instead. No food processor needed either. Just crumble cornbread with hand, make sure bread is stale or toasted and tear into chunks vs doing all crumbs. Came out great!

This recipe is a good start, but if following the recipe exactly, I would rate it a 3-4 star recipe...it's too soupy, and not nearly enough cornbread or flavor. I've made some changes to turn it into a 5 star recipe. In fact, with these changes, this is by far the best stuffing recipe I've ever had! Modifications: 1) Crumble and use 1lb of cornbread. 2) Reduce bread to 8 pieces (I prefer sourdough bread). 3) Use 1 onion, 5-6 celery stalks, and 1 green pepper very finely chopped.4) Cut butter to 1/2 cup. 5) Increase sage to 1 Tbsp, 6) Use sage sausage 7) Cook at 350. 8) Reduce to 1.5 to 2 cups of stock. 8) Add 2-3 hard boiled eggs.

I used 2 c of chicken stock instead of 4 based on comments I read from others. I used pkge of cornbread, cut into 1/2 in cubes and dried in oven at 350 for about 20 mins, and one pkge of potato bread cubes. I drained the veggie mixture a bit after cooking as it seemed like too much liquid. I baked it at 350 for about 1.30. It was moist but not soggy.

Excellent! Made this a couple of weeks before Thanksgiving as a test. Glad I did because I found out a few things. The cornbread should either be made from scratch or find a brand that does not use sugar. It was too sweet using the most popular cornbread mix. This type of dressing should not be sweet at all IMO. Also I chopped the celery too big. Another thing I discovered was the amount of chicken stock was dead on contrary to other reviews. I used a 32 ounce (4 cups) box of broth and it was perfect! The only thing I can think of that other reviewers are doing is not using enough bread. I use 16 slices of Butternut (keeping the crust) and had no problem at all with the dressing being soupy. It was moist and delicious. In sum, I would make my own cornbread with NO sugar in it. And chop the celery super fine via the food processor. And keep the stock at 4 cups. Doing this made my second batch pure heaven. My mom said it was better than hers and she was right (and I didn't think that was possible).

Good basic recipe but make your own cornbread and skip the mix. The preservatives in the mix give the "stove top" "right from the box" taste that some have complained about. Buy good quality, stone-ground corn meal, (Bob's Red Mill, etc) follow the simple recipe on the bag, and you will be so pleased with the flavor of your cornbread that you will never buy a mix again. Make a large enough batch that some of the cornbread can be the cook's breakfast while the rest goes into the stuffing. 
 Warm buttered cornbread makes getting up in the wee hours to prepare the holiday feast much more enjoyable.
(if you are a baker, make your own baguettes or whole wheat bread for the white bread portion of the recipe. I freeze a leftover baguettes and bread "heels." Double wrapped, they keep frozen for 3 months. You then eliminate all the bread preservatives and your stuffing will really taste like "Grandmother used to make.")

I love the flavor of this stuffing, but it was incredibly mushy. Whether you use a cornbread mix or a cornbread recipe, DO NOT use a recipe that is sweet or the stuffing will be very sweet. Make sure your bread is either well toasted or stale before sending it through your processor. Be sure to add your broth slowly (1/2 cup at a time). When you're finished adding it all together, the mixture will be moist - not wet and certainly not soggy.

Time-consuming for sure, but so delicious. Be sure to allow time for both the toasting of the bread cubes (40-60 minutes) and the 1 hour for baking the whole thing. I eliminate the bell pepper - just a personal preference. I sometimes make it vegetarian by substituting chopped mushrooms for the pork sausage and vegetable stock for the chicken stock.

After reviewing comments about mushy wet dressing I made 4 cups of billion. But put in only three as it looked like it would be enough. I also added 8 Oz. of mushrooms to the vegetables because they needed to be used. Turned out great.

27 Nov. 2024: Amazing recipe! Everything you would want in a crowd-pleaser. Instead of making a batch of cornbread, I used a 12 oz. bag of Corn Bread Classic Stuffing. Followed the recipe for everything else. The completed mix fit perfectly in a 9x13 pan. This is my new go-to dressing recipe. Prepared it today for our family Thanksgiving dinner tomorrow. This recipe is another thing to be thankful for....thank you for sharing it!

This is the closest recipe I can find to the one I make every year, except one year, I accidentally mixed it up with another recipe and ended up doing 4 boxes of cornbread instead of the 1 mentioned in this recipe. It came out more like a bread (think of a pan of brownies, but made of dressing), and to my surprise everyone liked it better that way, so that is how I make it every year now.

I have been making this recipe every Thanksgiving for 5 or 6 years now and its always a hit! for the most part I make it as it is written with the exceptions being that I add dried cranberries for a little sweet note to go with the salty and also I use fresh sliced Italian bread instead of white bread. This gives it a little more body and less mushy than regular white bread. Great Recipe!
This was a Thanksgiving hit! Delicious. The only change I made was to substitute store bought dried bread 'dressing' for the bread.
Really delicious but a tad too much butter for me
I did reduce the quantity of chicken broth and added in some chopped pecans. This was a fabulous dressing recipe, and quite tasty as well!
I had to change a few things for my family, but great recipe! I feel like I finally know how to make stuffing/ dressing. Thank you!

Not a crumb was left in the pan! I had never before made dressing from scratch, so I followed the recipe very closely. I cut up a loaf of grocery store french bread and dried it in a 250 degree oven for 15 minutes. I used all of the ingredients as listed and used the recipe's assembly method. I refrigerated it overnight. The recipe called for an hour's cooking time, but I extended it by ten minutes due to it's being refrigerated. I took it out, checked the internal temperature, took it next door and served it. I'm happy to say it was a hit and brought home an empty 9 x 13 glass pan. Thank you for a great recipe!
